subject: Geopolitics
title: Rare Earths: China's Hidden Leverage
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Rare Earths: China's Hidden Leverage.

hook.text: China processes 90% of the world's rare earth elements. Without them, no iPhones, no missiles, no wind turbines.

buildup.text: Rare earths aren't rare — they're hard to process. China invested decades in refining capacity others ignored.

discovery.text: This gives China a chokehold on high-tech manufacturing. A single export ban could cripple Western defense and tech.

twist.text: When China restricted rare earths in 2010 Japan fast-tracked recycling and alternative sources. Dependence shrank.

climax.text: The US, EU, and Australia are racing to build their own supply chains. But catching up takes a decade at minimum.

punchline.text: The raw material nobody noticed became everyone's weakness.

quiz.question: Why does China dominate rare earth processing?
options: China has the only deposits of rare earth minerals
China invested decades in refining capacity others neglected
International treaties gave China exclusive mining rights
